cohort: 168,784 mother-child pairs in India from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-IV) conducted in 2015-16.
finding: Several factors, including maternal age, education, cesarean section delivery, infant birth size, household wealth, and place of residence were associated with triple burden of malnutrition among mother-child pairs.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was associated with triple burden of malnutrition.
birth_weight: Birth size of baby was measured, but specific weights are not provided.
